timings.text: How to decline respectfully
Back to BHW Corazon.
Now that she knows the basis, how should she tell the company representative, without it sounding like a personal attack?
The right approach: first acknowledge the visitor's good intention, then explain the policy directly and clearly — not stalling, not pretending not to know.
"I understand you want to help, but we're not allowed to promote milk substitutes inside the BHS, under the Milk Code.
We also can't take samples, gifts or other offers from milk companies.
I'll let our midwife know you came by."
Corazon does not suggest any other way for the company to help, and she promises nothing in return.
That same day she tells the midwife about the visit.
The strongest refusal isn't an angry one — it's clear, has a basis, makes no deal, and is reported to the midwife.
Paano tumanggi nang magalang
Bumalik tayo kay BHW Corazon.
Ngayong alam na niya ang batayan, paano niya sasabihin ito sa kinatawan ng kumpanya nang hindi nagmukhang personal na pag-atake?
Ang tamang paraan: kilalanin muna ang mabuting intensyon ng bisita, saka ipaliwanag ang polisiya nang direkta at malinaw — hindi pagpapaliban, hindi pagpapanggap na hindi alam.
"Naiintindihan ko po ang gusto ninyong tumulong, pero bawal po sa amin ang mag-promote ng milk substitute sa loob ng BHS, ayon sa Milk Code.
Hindi rin po kami puwedeng tumanggap ng sample, regalo, o iba pang alok mula sa kumpanya ng gatas.
Sasabihin ko po sa aming midwife na dumaan kayo."
Hindi nagmumungkahi si Corazon ng ibang paraan para tumulong ang kumpanya, at wala siyang ipinapangakong kapalit.
Sa araw ding iyon, sinasabihan niya ang midwife tungkol sa pagbisita.
Ang pinakamalakas na pagtanggi ay hindi galit — ito ay malinaw, may batayan, walang kasunduan, at ipinaaalam sa midwife.
Wrong versus right: the company's offer
**Wrong**: BHW Danilo accepted the samples and gifts from the medicine company's representative, because "it's free anyway, and maybe it's rude to say no."
He handed the samples out to patients with no explanation of why they were being recommended.
**Right**: Corazon respectfully declined, explained the basis in the Milk Code, made no deal of any kind with the company, and told the midwife about the visit that same day.
The difference isn't kindness or its absence — the difference is who gets to decide what's good for the patient: the BHS, guided by policy, or the company, guided by its own benefit.
When an offer is accepted with no basis behind it, it is the company, not the BHS, that ends up deciding what's good for the patient.
Mali kumpara sa tama: ang alok ng kumpanya
**Mali**: Tinanggap ni BHW Danilo ang mga sample at regalo mula sa kinatawan ng kumpanya ng gamot, dahil "libre naman, at baka magkasala pa ako kung tatanggihan ko."
Ipinamigay niya ang mga sample sa mga pasyente nang walang paliwanag kung bakit ito ang inirekomenda.

**Tama**: Magalang na tumanggi si Corazon, ipinaliwanag ang batayan mula sa Milk Code, walang pinasok na anumang kasunduan sa kumpanya, at sinabihan ang midwife tungkol sa pagbisita sa araw ding iyon.
Ang pagkakaiba ay hindi kabaitan o kawalan nito — ang pagkakaiba ay kung sino ang nagpapasya kung ano ang mabuti para sa pasyente: ang BHS batay sa polisiya, o ang kumpanya batay sa benepisyo nito.
Kapag tinanggap ang alok nang walang batayan, ang kumpanya na, hindi ang BHS, ang nagpapasya kung ano ang mabuti para sa pasyente.
One efficient suggestion

Try it: think of one thing at your own barangay health station that could be made more efficient — for example, a light left on with no one around, water dripping unnoticed, or plastics that shouldn't be used any more under DC 2021-0486.
Write your suggestion as one sentence you could actually say to the midwife or a fellow BHW — not just "we should change," but exactly what to change and why it would help.
A suggestion that's specific and has a reason is far more likely to be believed and actually carried out than a general complaint.
Isang mungkahing episyente

Subukan mo: mag-isip ng isang bagay sa iyong barangay health station na kayang gawing mas episyente — halimbawa, ang ilaw na naiiwang bukas kahit walang tao, o ang tubig na tumutulo nang hindi napapansin, o ang mga plastic na hindi na dapat ginagamit ayon sa DC 2021-0486.
Isulat ang mungkahi mo sa isang pangungusap na kaya mong sabihin sa midwife o sa kapwa BHW — hindi lang "dapat magbago," kundi tiyak na kung ano ang babaguhin at bakit ito makakatulong.
Ang mungkahing tiyak at may dahilan ang mas malamang na paniwalaan at tuluyang maisagawa kaysa sa pangkalahatang reklamo.
The visitor at the BHS
A representative from a milk company arrived at BHW Corazon's barangay health station — carrying samples and a tarpaulin showing their new product.
"Could we leave these inside, for you to give out to the mothers?
We also have a small gift for you."
Corazon knew she had to decline — but how could she do it without offending the visitor, and with the right reasoning behind her refusal?
Declining isn't just about "I don't want to" — there's a policy behind it, and the refusal is stronger once you know what that basis is.
Ang bisita sa BHS
May dumating na kinatawan ng isang kumpanya ng gatas sa barangay health station ni BHW Corazon — may dalang mga sample at tarpaulin na nagpapakita ng kanilang bagong produkto.
"Puwede po bang ilagay namin ito sa loob, at ipamigay ninyo sa mga nanay?
May konting regalo din po kami para sa inyo."
Alam ni Corazon na kailangan niyang tumanggi — pero paano niya ito gagawin nang hindi masamang loob ang bisita, at nang tama ang dahilan niya sa pagtanggi?
Ang pagtanggi ay hindi lang tungkol sa "ayaw ko" — may batayan itong polisiya, at mas malakas ito kapag alam mo ang batayang iyon.
Two bans on promotion
The Milk Code (EO 51) restricts promotion of covered breastmilk substitutes in the health-care system and inducements to health workers.
Do not accept gifts in exchange for promoting such products.
Pharmaceutical promotion also has ethical rules: the source training material cites DOH AO 2015-0053.
Do not treat all industry interactions as identical or independently approve a promotion.
Refer the offer to the facility supervisor and check the current policy.
The exact scope and exceptions of this order still require primary-source review before this draft is published.
The product differs — milk on one side, medicine on the other — but the principle is the same: no company should be able to influence the service given inside a barangay health station.
Dalawang bawal sa promosyon
Nililimitahan ng Milk Code (EO 51) ang promosyon ng saklaw na breastmilk substitutes sa health-care system at mga insentibo sa health workers.
Huwag tumanggap ng regalo kapalit ng pagpromote ng mga produktong ito.
May etikang tuntunin din sa pharmaceutical promotion: binabanggit ng pinagmulang materyal ang DOH AO 2015-0053.
Huwag ituring na magkakapareho ang lahat ng pakikipag-ugnayan sa industriya o mag-apruba ng promosyon nang mag-isa.
Idulog ang alok sa namamahala at tiyakin ang kasalukuyang polisiya.
Kailangan pang repasuhin ang eksaktong saklaw at exceptions sa pangunahing sanggunian bago ilathala ang draft na ito.
Magkaiba ang produkto — gatas sa isa, gamot sa isa — pero iisa ang prinsipyo: walang kumpanya ang dapat makaimpluwensya sa serbisyong ibinibigay sa loob ng barangay health station.
Other policies and using resources efficiently

Beyond the four policies you just learned, this competency — *practice entrepreneurial skills in the workplace* — also covers a broader skill: knowing the workplace's policies and structure, finding ways to make electricity, water, and supplies use more efficient, and being resourceful in the face of limited resources.
This isn't separate from the four policies — it's the same skill: the ability to look at a situation, spot a better way, and explain it clearly to others.
Declining the offer to Corazon is one way of using it; proposing a more efficient way to use resources is another.
The same skill — spotting a better way and explaining it clearly — is what's used both to decline an offer and to propose a change at the workplace.
Iba pang polisiya at episyenteng paggamit ng resources

Bukod sa apat na polisiyang natutunan mo, saklaw din ng kakayahang ito — *practice entrepreneurial skills in the workplace* — ang mas malawak na kasanayan: alamin ang mga polisiya at istruktura ng lugar ng trabaho, tumukoy ng paraan para gawing mas episyente ang paggamit ng kuryente, tubig, at gamit, at maging mapamaraan sa harap ng limitadong rekurso.
Hindi ito hiwalay sa apat na polisiya — kaparehong kasanayan ito: ang kakayahang tumingin sa isang sitwasyon, tumukoy ng mas mahusay na paraan, at maipaliwanag ito nang malinaw sa iba.
Ang pagtanggi kay Corazon ay isang paraan ng paggamit nito; ang pagmungkahi ng mas episyenteng paraan ng paggamit ng resources ay isa pang paraan.
Ang parehong kasanayan — pagtukoy ng mas mahusay na paraan at pagpapaliwanag nito nang malinaw — ang gamit sa pagtanggi sa isang alok at sa pagmumungkahi ng pagbabago sa lugar ng trabaho.
Promoting breastfeeding, and the ban on plastic
RA 10028 strengthens breastfeeding support, including lactation stations under its requirements.
A BHW can direct a parent to trained support and help maintain a respectful, supportive environment.
DOH DC 2021-0486 concerns phased restrictions on unnecessary single-use plastics in health facilities and DOH offices.
Follow facility guidance on safe alternatives.
Do not remove sterile or otherwise necessary clinical supplies on your own; reducing unnecessary waste must not compromise safe care.
These policies aren't just about prohibition — they also expect active follow-through: promote breastfeeding, cut down on plastic.
Pagsusulong sa breastfeeding at pagbabawal sa plastic
Pinalalakas ng RA 10028 ang suporta sa breastfeeding, kasama ang lactation stations ayon sa mga tuntunin nito.
Maaaring ituro ng BHW ang magulang sa sinanay na tagasuporta at tumulong sa magalang at suportadong kapaligiran.
Tungkol ang DOH DC 2021-0486 sa phased restrictions sa hindi kailangang single-use plastics sa health facilities at DOH offices.
Sundin ang gabay ng pasilidad sa ligtas na alternatibo.
Huwag mag-alis nang mag-isa ng sterile o kinakailangang clinical supplies; hindi dapat makompromiso ang ligtas na pangangalaga sa pagbabawas ng basura.
Ang mga polisiyang ito ay hindi lang tungkol sa pagbabawal — may aktibong inaasahan din: isulong ang breastfeeding, bawasan ang plastic.
Who makes up the accreditation process

The local health board does not simply grant accreditation on a whim — it carries a set of responsibilities under Section 5 of the RA 7883 IRR: safeguard the registration and accreditation process, evaluate applications, record decisions in a board resolution or meeting minutes, issue certificates of registration or accreditation, review and approve any benefit that would use local funds, recommend benefits and fund appropriation, provide an official copy of the BHW registry to the DOH, and monitor the service registered BHWs provide.
The local health board may also create a BHW Registration and Accreditation Committee to evaluate applications, interview applicants, recommend action to the board, and keep the BHW registry updated.
Accreditation isn't decided by one person alone — it runs through a system, with assigned responsibility and a registry that's kept up to date.
Kung sino ang bumubuo sa proseso ng akreditasyon

Hindi basta-basta pumapayag ang local health board sa akreditasyon — may hanay ng responsibilidad ito ayon sa Section 5 ng RA 7883 IRR: pangalagaan ang proseso ng rehistrasyon at akreditasyon, suriin ang mga aplikasyon, itala ang desisyon sa isang board resolution o minutes ng pulong, maglabas ng certificate of registration o accreditation, suriin at aprubahan ang bawat benepisyong gagamit ng pondong lokal, magrekomenda ng benepisyo at pondo, magbigay ng opisyal na kopya ng BHW registry sa DOH, at bantayan ang serbisyong ibinibigay ng mga rehistradong BHW.

Maaari ring lumikha ang local health board ng isang BHW Registration and Accreditation Committee na susuri ng mga aplikasyon, kakapanayamin ang mga aplikante, magrerekomenda sa local health board, at mag-uupdate ng BHW registry.
Hindi iisang tao lang ang nagpapasya sa akreditasyon — may sistema ito, may itinalagang responsibilidad, at may talaang pinapanatili.
Why each relationship matters
If BHW Marites always went to the midwife for everything, everything would slow down — the midwife's time would fill up with things that were never clinical to begin with.
If she never built a relationship with barangay officials, she would struggle to get support when she needed transport or supplies.
If she never connected with fellow BHWs, she would stay alone with experiences that should have been learned together.
Each relationship has its own purpose — and using the right one at the right moment is what makes barangay service fast and reliable.
Each relationship has its own purpose — using the right one at the right moment is what makes service fast and reliable.
Bakit mahalaga ang bawat ugnayan
Kung palagi na lamang lalapitan ni BHW Marites ang midwife para sa lahat ng bagay, mabagal ang lahat — mapupuno ang oras ng midwife sa mga bagay na hindi naman klinikal.
Kung hindi naman siya kikilala sa barangay officials, mahihirapan siyang humingi ng suporta kapag kailangan ng transportasyon o kagamitan.
Kung hindi siya nakikipag-ugnayan sa kapwa BHW, mananatili siyang mag-isa sa mga karanasang dapat sana ay napag-aaralan nang magkasama.
Bawat ugnayan ay may sariling layunin — at ang paggamit ng tamang ugnayan sa tamang pagkakataon ang gumagawa sa serbisyo ng barangay na mabilis at maaasahan.
Ang bawat ugnayan ay may sariling layunin — ang paggamit ng tama sa tamang pagkakataon ang gumagawa sa serbisyo na mabilis at maaasahan.
Additional contacts within the barangay
Beyond the four relationships, there are two more contacts within the barangay itself that BHW Marites should know.

The **punong barangay** is the BHW's partner in carrying out the barangay's mandate to provide basic health services, and oversees BHWs administratively — for the health work itself, the midwife remains the BHW's technical supervisor.
They also decide how the barangay budget is used — including BHW honoraria.
The **Kagawad sa Kalusugan** advocates health policies and resolutions in the barangay council, and is also a member of the barangay planning team for health.
They push for budget for health-related activities, facilities, and materials.
The punong barangay holds the budget; the Kagawad sa Kalusugan advocates for policy. Different roles, both worth knowing.
Karagdagang kakilala sa barangay
Bukod sa apat na ugnayan, may dalawa pang kakilala sa loob mismo ng barangay na dapat malaman ni BHW Marites.

Ang **punong barangay** ay ka-partner ng mga BHW sa pagpapatupad ng mandato nitong magbigay ng basic health services, at administratibong nangangasiwa sa mga BHW — sa mismong gawaing pangkalusugan, ang midwife pa rin ang teknikal na supervisor ng BHW.
Siya rin ang nagdedesisyon kung paano gagamitin ang budget ng barangay — kasama ang pagbibigay ng honorarium para sa mga BHW.
Ang **kagawad sa kalusugan** naman ang tagapagtaguyod sa konseho ng barangay ng mga polisiya at resolusyong pangkalusugan, at miyembro rin siya ng barangay planning team for health.
Siya ang nagsusulong ng budget para sa mga gawain, pasilidad, at materyales na may kinalaman sa kalusugan.
Ang punong barangay ang may hawak ng budget; ang kagawad sa kalusugan ang tagapagtaguyod ng polisiya. Magkaiba ang papel, pareho silang kailangang kakilala.
The benefits under RA 7883

RA 7883 names specific benefits a BHW may receive: hazard allowance, subsistence allowance (for BHWs who serve at isolated barangay health stations), training and career enrichment programs, civil service eligibility, free legal services, and priority access to loans.
The amounts are set locally: the hazard allowance by the local health board and the local peace and order council, and the subsistence allowance by the LGU.
There is a condition before becoming eligible for these: a BHW must be registered with the local health board of the city or municipality where they render service.

There is also a limit: the total number of BHWs nationwide must not exceed one percent (1%) of the country's population, and the DOH sets the ideal number of BHWs per household — so registration is not simply given to anyone, and getting it right matters.
These benefits have specific conditions and administrative procedures.
Confirm eligibility, documentation and any locally funded allowance with the local health board; do not promise automatic or uniform payment.
These benefits aren't automatic — they depend on proper registration with the local health board.
Ang mga benepisyo sa ilalim ng RA 7883

Kasama sa RA 7883 ang mga partikular na benepisyong maaaring matanggap ng isang BHW: hazard allowance, subsistence allowance (para sa BHW na naglilingkod sa isolated o liblib na barangay health station), mga programa sa pagsasanay at career enrichment, civil service eligibility, libreng legal services, at priority access sa mga loan o pautang.
Lokal na itinatakda ang halaga: ang hazard allowance ng local health board at ng local peace and order council, at ang subsistence allowance ng LGU.
May kondisyon bago maging eligible dito: kailangang rehistrado ang BHW sa local health board ng lungsod o munisipyo kung saan siya nagbibigay ng serbisyo.

May limitasyon din: ang kabuuang bilang ng mga BHW sa buong bansa ay hindi dapat lumampas sa isang porsiyento (1%) ng populasyon ng bansa, at ang DOH ang nagtatakda ng angkop na bilang ng BHW kada dami ng sambahayan — kaya't hindi basta-basta tinatanggap ang lahat, at mahalaga ang tamang rehistrasyon.
May tiyak na kondisyon at prosesong administratibo ang mga benepisyong ito.
Tiyakin sa local health board ang pagiging kwalipikado, dokumento, at allowance na lokal ang pondo; huwag mangako ng awtomatiko o pare-parehong bayad.
Ang mga benepisyong ito ay hindi awtomatiko — nakasalalay ito sa tamang rehistrasyon sa local health board.
Apply your learning
Which is a clear organizing action?
Connect people, invite action, and bring observations into planning.
Gamitin ang natutuhan
Alin ang malinaw na gawaing pang-organisa?
Mag-ugnay ng tao, mag-anyaya ng pagkilos, at dalhin ang obserbasyon sa pagpaplano.
Contribute to wider planning
The Local Investment Plan for Health, or LIPH, is the city or provincial health plan described in the manual.
It recognizes barangay and municipal contributions to planning.
Observations shared by BHWs can inform discussion of local needs.
Contribute through the existing local process with the health team; a proposal does not automatically receive funding.
Local Investment Plan for Health: barangays contribute; confirm the local process.
May ambag sa mas malawak na plano
Ang Local Investment Plan for Health o LIPH ay planong pangkalusugan sa antas ng lungsod o probinsya na tinutukoy ng manual.
Kinikilala rito ang kontribusyon ng barangay at munisipyo sa pagpaplano.
Ang obserbasyong ibinahagi ng BHW ay maaaring makatulong sa pagtalakay ng mga lokal na pangangailangan.
Ipaalam sa health team ang ambag sa pamamagitan ng umiiral na lokal na proseso; hindi awtomatikong pondado ang bawat mungkahi.
Local Investment Plan for Health: may ambag ang barangay; kumpirmahin ang lokal na proseso.
From observation to conversation
Marites notices standing water in some yards.
She talks with residents, the purok leader, the health council member, and health staff about a possible shared activity.
A Community Organizer maintains good relationships and communication with the community and city or municipal health staff.
Relationships and communication begin collective action.
Mula obserbasyon, tungo sa usapan
Napansin ni Marites ang naipong tubig sa ilang bakuran.
Kinausap niya ang mga residente, purok leader, kagawad sa kalusugan, at health staff tungkol sa posibleng sama-samang gawain.
Ang Community Organizer ay nagpapanatili ng mabuting relasyon at komunikasyon sa komunidad at sa health staff ng lungsod o munisipyo.
Ugnayan at komunikasyon ang simula ng sama-samang pagkilos.
Invite people to participate
Marites does more than announce a clean-up drive.
She asks who can join, what they can contribute, and which schedule is possible.
A clear invitation names an action, includes partners, and allows people to respond.
Residents participate rather than simply watch.
Listen to responses; shape the activity with residents.
Anyayahang makilahok
Hindi lang ipinapaalam ni Marites na may clean-up drive.
Tinatanong niya kung sino ang makasasama, ano ang kaya nilang gawin, at anong iskedyul ang posible.
Ang malinaw na paanyaya ay may gagawin, kasama, at pagkakataong sumagot.
Ang mga residente ay kalahok sa gawain, hindi tagapanood lamang.
Makinig sa tugon; buuin ang gawain kasama ang mga residente.
Bring observations into planning
The manual describes the BHW as part of the barangay planning team for health.
The BHW brings relevant observations to help leaders understand and act on a problem.
Separate what was seen from an assumption: “There is standing water in three yards” is an observation; it does not prove the cause of an illness.
Share evidence without presenting assumptions as established facts.
Dalhin ang nakita sa pagpaplano
Inilalarawan ng manual ang BHW bilang bahagi ng barangay planning team for health.
Dinadala niya ang kaugnay na obserbasyon upang matulungan ang mga lider na maunawaan at aksyunan ang problema.
Ihiwalay ang aktuwal na nakita sa hinala: “May naipong tubig sa tatlong bakuran” ay obserbasyon; hindi pa iyon patunay na iyon ang sanhi ng isang sakit.
Ibahagi ang ebidensya, hindi ang hinalang parang tiyak na katotohanan.
BHW Eligibility (BHWE) in the Civil Service
There is a separate qualification for BHW Eligibility under the Civil Service Commission (CSC Resolution No.

Four conditions are required: accredited by the local health board; completed a minimum of two (2) years of college leading to a degree; actively and voluntarily serving continuously, full time, for five (5) years or more as an accredited BHW; and having a satisfactory service record as an accredited BHW in the community.
The five years count only if the service was voluntary — no salary or other pay except an honorarium for the whole period — and only from the time the BHW was already accredited.
Service before 20 February 1995, when RA 7883 was approved, does not count.
A BHW hired under a job order or contract of service can still qualify.
This is not the same thing as general accreditation — it asks for more, and it is for BHWs who want official eligibility in the civil service.

BHWE needs four conditions — accreditation, two years of college, five years of continuous, full-time voluntary service as an accredited BHW, and a satisfactory record. Missing even one means it isn't met yet.
Ang BHW Eligibility (BHWE) sa Civil Service
May hiwalay na kwalipikasyon para sa BHW Eligibility sa ilalim ng Civil Service Commission (CSC Resolution No.

Apat na kondisyon ang kailangan: akreditado ng local health board; nakatapos ng minimum na dalawang (2) taon sa kolehiyo tungo sa isang degree; aktibo at boluntaryong naglilingkod nang tuloy-tuloy at full time sa loob ng limang (5) taon o higit pa bilang accredited BHW; at may satisfactory service bilang accredited BHW sa komunidad.
Bibilangin lang ang limang taon kung boluntaryo ang serbisyo — walang sahod o ibang bayad maliban sa honorarium sa buong panahon — at mula lamang nang akreditado na ang BHW.
Hindi binibilang ang serbisyo bago ang 20 Pebrero 1995, nang maaprubahan ang RA 7883.
Maaari pa ring mag-qualify ang BHW na naka-job order o contract of service.
Hindi ito parehong bagay sa pangkalahatang akreditasyon — mas mataas ang hinihingi nito, at para ito sa mga BHW na nais magkaroon ng opisyal na eligibility sa serbisyo sibil.

Apat na kondisyon ang kailangan sa BHWE — akreditasyon, dalawang taon sa kolehiyo, limang taon ng tuloy-tuloy, full-time at boluntaryong serbisyo bilang accredited BHW, at satisfactory service. Kulang ang isa, hindi pa ito matutugunan.
When the process is slow
You now know the whole process — but what do you do if months pass with no word?
The best move: calm yourself first before frustration takes over, then follow up with a specific question — not "when will this be done?"
but "what's the status of my application, and is there anything else I need to submit?"
A clear, calm question is more likely to get answered than a complaint with no specific ask.
Following up calmly and with a specific question works better than a complaint with no specific ask.
Kapag mabagal ang proseso
Alam mo na ngayon ang buong proseso — pero ano ang gagawin mo kung inabot ito ng ilang buwan nang walang balita?
Ang pinakamahusay na hakbang: pakalmahin muna ang sarili bago sumulpot sa galit, saka mag-follow-up nang may tiyak na tanong — hindi "kailan pa ba ito matatapos?"
kundi "ano pong status ng aking aplikasyon, at may kailangan pa po ba akong ibigay?"
Ang malinaw at kalmadong tanong ay mas malamang na masagot kaysa sa reklamong walang tiyak na hinihingi.
Ang pag-follow-up nang kalmado at may tiyak na tanong ay mas epektibo kaysa sa reklamong walang tiyak na hinihingi.
Wrong versus right: following up on a benefit
**Wrong**: Josie waited six months for her accreditation but never asked, because "maybe I'll look impatient."
She eventually found out one of her documents had gone missing at the office — a six-month delay that could have been avoided with an earlier follow-up.
**Right**: Josie followed up every two months, with a specific question about her application's status, and reminded them calmly whenever needed.
When the missing document was discovered, it was resubmitted right away.
Staying silent in the face of a delay isn't politeness — it often just lets a problem drag on that could have been fixed much sooner.
Mali kumpara sa tama: humingi ng nararapat
**Mali**: Anim na buwan nang naghihintay si Josie sa kanyang akreditasyon, pero hindi siya nagtanong kahit kailan dahil "baka mukhang naiinip ako."
Sa kalaunan, nalaman niyang nawala pala ang isa sa kanyang mga dokumento sa opisina — anim na buwang pagkaantala na naiwasan sana kung nag-follow-up siya nang maaga.
**Tama**: Nag-follow-up si Josie tuwing dalawang buwan, may tiyak na tanong tungkol sa status ng aplikasyon, at kalmadong nagpaalala tuwing kailangan.
Nang matuklasan ang nawawalang dokumento, agad itong naibigay muli.
Ang katahimikan sa harap ng pagkaantala ay hindi pagiging magalang — madalas itong nagpapahaba lang ng problemang kaya sanang naayos nang maaga.
Reach every community group
Education must reach beyond people who already attend a health talk.
Consider who is missing: children, young people, older adults, and other groups in the barangay.
Choose a time, place, language, and format that support participation.
Offer information, knowledge, and opportunities to practise.
Information, knowledge, and training for every community group.
Abutin ang bawat sektor
Hindi lamang ang mga dumadalo na sa health talk ang kailangang maabot.
Pag-isipan kung sino ang hindi nakakasali: mga bata, kabataan, nakatatanda, at iba pang grupo sa barangay.
Pumili ng oras, lugar, wika, at paraan na makatutulong sa kanila na makilahok.
Magbigay ng impormasyon, kaalaman, at pagkakataong magsanay.
Impormasyon, kaalaman, at pagsasanay para sa bawat sektor.

Where the BHW's duty comes from
A BHW's status as a voluntary frontliner is not simply assumed — it is written into law.
Under Republic Act 7883, a BHW "voluntarily renders primary health care services" in the community after receiving proper training and accreditation from the local health board.
This is also where the Primary Health Care Approach as the guiding strategy comes from, and why the barangay health station exists as a service hub.
In other words: a BHW is not a "volunteer" in the everyday sense only — their duty has a legal basis, and that is also why an accreditation process exists before the work can begin.
The BHW's duty has a legal basis — it is not just goodwill, it is part of RA 7883.
Saan nanggagaling ang tungkulin ng BHW
Ang katayuan ng BHW bilang boluntaryong frontliner ay hindi basta-basta naitalaga — nasa batas ito.
Ayon sa Republic Act 7883, ang BHW ay "boluntaryong nagbibigay ng primary health care services sa komunidad" matapos makatanggap ng tamang pagsasanay at akreditasyon mula sa local health board.
Dito rin nakabatay ang paggamit ng Primary Health Care Approach bilang pangunahing estratehiya, at ang pagkakaroon ng barangay health station bilang sentro ng serbisyo.

Sa madaling salita: hindi lang "boluntir" sa pangkaraniwang kahulugan ang BHW — may legal na batayan ang kanilang tungkulin, at ito rin ang dahilan kung bakit may proseso ng akreditasyon bago simulan ang gawain.

Additional contacts at the city or municipal level
The barangay opens up into a wider network once you reach the city or municipal level.
The **City or Municipal Health Officer (CHO/MHO)** is the overall manager of health for the whole city or town, and the general supervisor of health workers including BHWs.
The **midwife**, assigned to the barangay health station, sets the BHW's tasks and is their technical supervisor.
The **Public Health Nurse (PHN)** supervises the midwives, and is sometimes assigned as supervisor of all BHWs citywide.

There is a new level to meet as well: the **city or municipal-level HEPO office** — not the same as a BHW's own HEPO designation (which you already learned in Module 1), but the office that plans health promotion for the whole locality and monitors BHWs' skill at it.
And the **local health board**, which gives health recommendations to the LGU and manages the budget — the mayor chairs it, the CHO/MHO is vice-chair.
As the level rises — barangay, city, municipality — the number of people connected to the health service you provide grows too.

Other partners
Four more partners round out BHW Marites' network.

Four relationships of a BHW
A BHW's work does not revolve around just one person.
Four relationships shape the day-to-day work: The **community** — families like Aling Nena's, where the first step of care happens.
The **midwife or Rural Health Unit (RHU)** — the technical support the BHW turns to for referrals or clinical questions.
The **barangay officials** — the partner for support and facilities like the barangay health station.
(Accreditation itself comes from the local health board of the city or municipality, as Module 4 explains.)
And **fellow BHWs** — the peers who share experience and correct practice.
These are four distinct relationships, but they are always present together in an ordinary BHW day.
Four relationships run through the BHW — the role never works alone.

How to improve self-management
These skills aren't natural to everyone — but there are specific ways to develop them.
Practice self-care, since stress lowers performance.
Train yourself to be patient, since everyone has their own timeline.
Finish one task at a time, since multitasking doesn't actually get more done.
Reflect on your own abilities — you improve faster once you know them.
Set specific, measurable, achievable, realistic, time-bound (SMART) goals.

Come to meetings prepared — ask for the agenda and read materials beforehand.
And think before you speak.

Self-management skills
Because each BHW is still just one person, they also need skills aimed inward — not only skills for relating to others.

Six skills matter: being **reliable** — delivering the good service expected of them; **stress management** — staying calm and focused under pressure; **time management** — prioritizing what matters so work finishes on time; being **trustworthy** — holding to principles and moral standards; **adaptability** — willing to accept and keep up with change; and being **honest and careful** — thoughtful in what is said and how others are treated.

What good teamwork looks like
A barangay usually has more than one BHW, and they need to work as a team.
Five recommendations guide this.

The goal of the UHC Act
The Universal Health Care Act of 2019 (RA 11223) aims to improve access to quality health services and protect people from financial hardship.
It automatically includes every Filipino in the National Health Insurance Program.
This does not mean every service at every facility is free.
Contribution obligations and rules for accessing particular benefits still apply.
Help the resident verify the relevant benefit, provider and registration process with PhilHealth or the RHU.
UHC's direction is clear: from a system that waits for someone to pay, to one that guarantees service everyone can reach.

Layunin ng Universal Health Care Act of 2019 (RA 11223) ang mas madaling paglapit sa dekalidad na serbisyo at proteksiyon laban sa mabigat na gastusin.
Awtomatikong kasama ang bawat Pilipino sa National Health Insurance Program.
Hindi nito ibig sabihing libre ang bawat serbisyo sa bawat pasilidad.

Ang direksyon ng UHC ay malinaw: mula sa sistemang umaasang may babayad, tungo sa sistemang nagsisiguro na may serbisyong maaabot ang lahat.

The health board and the BHW's part in moving it forward
UHC also brings a new partner: the **provincial or city health board**, tasked with helping organize and manage the health system at the provincial or city level.
Suggestions and concerns from the barangay can reach it, through the midwife and the municipal or city health office.
Because of these changes, a higher level of skill is also expected of BHWs, and health promotion within communities is intensified.
This is also why BHWs were designated HEPOs — you already learned this in detail in Module 1.

So the skill this calls for is not only knowing the law: it also means spotting the chance to improve how it is carried out, and getting that suggestion to the right person — a fellow BHW, the midwife, all the way up to the health board.
UHC does not just change the system — it also expects the BHW to contribute: observation, suggestion, and action.
Ang health board at ang papel ng BHW sa pagsulong
May bagong kasosyo rin ang UHC: ang **provincial o city health board**, na naatasang tumulong mag-organisa at mamahala sa sistemang pangkalusugan sa antas ng probinsya o lungsod.
Maaaring umabot dito ang mga mungkahi at hinaing mula sa barangay, sa pamamagitan ng midwife at ng municipal o city health office.
Dahil sa mga pagbabagong ito, inaasahan din ang mas mataas na antas ng kasanayan mula sa mga BHW, at mas pinaigting na health promotion sa komunidad.
Ito rin ang dahilan kung bakit itinalaga ang BHW bilang HEPO — natutunan mo na ito nang detalyado sa Modyul 1.

Kaya naman, ang kakayahang kailangan dito ay hindi lang malaman ang batas: kailangan ding matukoy ang pagkakataong mapabuti pa ang pagpapatupad nito, at maipaabot ang mungkahi sa tamang tao — sa kapwa BHW, sa midwife, hanggang sa umabot sa health board.
Ang UHC ay hindi lang nagbabago ng sistema — inaasahan din nitong may ibahagi ang BHW: obserbasyon, mungkahi, at aksyon.
Four concrete changes
UHC provides for stronger primary care, including outpatient benefits, registration with a primary care provider and coordinated referral to other services.
A primary care provider helps navigate care; the BHW supports the resident within their training and supervision.
Province-wide and city-wide health systems are intended to coordinate services.
Do not assume every service or referral arrangement is already available locally.
Check the current provider, benefit and referral procedure before advising a resident.
These four changes are connected — each one has to do with how a person moves from having a need to actually receiving service.

Tumutulong ang primary care provider sa pag-ugnay ng pangangalaga; ang BHW ay umaalalay ayon sa pagsasanay at pangangasiwa.
